title: Practice prediction: Tokyo Sports Hai Nisai Stakes (G2)
sub: Use a real race to try predicting and betting with ¥10,000 of virtual money. We will announce the result after watching the race video together.
how: Read the race conditions and the race card
Look at the odds and the "reasons for popularity"
Build your bets with ¥10,000 of virtual money
Watch the race video, enter the result and check your bets
race: 2-year-old Open, G2. Every horse carries the same 56kg
course: Tokyo has a long home straight of about 526m with a slope on the way. It is said to be a course where horses coming from behind can still catch up.
cardNote: Win odds are the final odds just before the start. "Crowd's win chance" = 80 ÷ odds: the chance of winning that the crowd believes, worked back from the odds (using the 80% payout rate). Added together, they come to about 100%.
whyLead: Horses are listed in order of popularity. Read why each horse is (or isn't) popular, and compare it with your own thinking.
reasons: Won a maiden race over the same Tokyo turf 1800m in a fast 1:46.7. The jockey is C. Lemaire, one of Japan's top jockeys.

Has just won a newcomer race at Tokyo over turf 2000m — only one career start. The winning time of 2:03.9 was slow, so people worried about the stronger rivals in a graded race. Likes to run in front (a front-runner).
Finished 5th in the Sapporo Nisai Stakes (G3). It was beaten by more than 1 second by that race's winner, No. 10 ショウナンガレオン, so it was seen as unlikely to win here.

Won a newcomer race at Hanshin over turf 1800m in 1:46.9. Popular combination of jockey Y. Kawada and the Nakauchida stable, known for strong 2-year-olds. But with only one start, it is still unknown.
Won a newcomer race over Tokyo turf 1800m, then was 3rd in the Fuyo Stakes (Open) on heavy ground. Some think it can do better on good ground. The jockey is J. Moreira, a world-class rider.
Won a maiden race at Hanshin over turf 1800m. It has never run in a graded or open race, and the rivals get much stronger, so it is not very popular.
Won a newcomer race at Nakayama over turf 1800m, but the time of 1:53.2 (slightly heavy ground) was slow, so its strength is still unclear.
Was 2nd in the Ivy Stakes (Open) over the same Tokyo turf 1800m. It started slowly but finished fast. People rate how well it suits this course.
Won a maiden race over Tokyo turf 1600m. The distance is 200m longer this time and it has no graded-race experience, so it is not very popular.
Won the Sapporo Nisai Stakes (G3) by 6 lengths — the only graded-race winner in the field. It also set a course record in its newcomer race. A clear favourite.
Has just won a newcomer race at Kyoto over turf 2000m — only one career start. The jockey is K. Tosaki, one of the top jockeys in eastern Japan.
Was 3rd in its newcomer race, then won a maiden race at Kyoto over turf 2000m. Another reason for attention: the veteran jockey Y. Take.
hints: Do you believe the "crowd's win chance"? Is any horse rated too high or too low?
Which horses have already run over the same Tokyo turf 1800m?
For horses changing distance, is the new distance good for them?
Has the horse run in graded or open races? Horses that just won a newcomer or maiden race face stronger rivals.
In the paddock video: does the horse look calm and in good condition?
simLead: You have ¥10,000 of virtual money. Choose a bet type and horses, enter an amount (in ¥100 units) and press "Add". You can combine as many bets as you like.
errSame: You chose the same horse (bracket) twice. Please choose different horses.
estNote: Win odds are the real final odds. Odds for other bet types are estimates calculated from the win odds and differ from the real payouts.
resH: Enter the result (after watching the race video)
resLead: Watch the race video together and listen to the teacher's announcement, then enter the 1st to 3rd horses. For winning tickets, enter the real payout announced (per ¥100) to get an exact result.
errRes: Please choose three different horses for 1st to 3rd.
estWarn: Tickets without an entered payout are calculated with the estimated odds.
reflect: Which popularity rank were your horses? Did you follow the crowd or go against it?
Was your return rate higher or lower than 80% (the payout rate)?
Which viewpoint helped? Which viewpoint do you want to check with data next?
Can one result tell you that a way of betting is right? How many races of data would you need to check it?
src: The race card and odds are based on JRA announcements and news reports. All money is virtual; we do not actually bet (betting is allowed from age 20).
pickHelp: Tap numbers to choose horses (brackets). If you choose several, you buy every combination at once.
